name: Olympiacos FC
content:
Olympiacos FC is a professional football club based in Piraeus, Greece, founded in 1925. It was created through the merger of local clubs and quickly became one of the most important teams in the country. The club’s identity is closely linked to its port-city roots and its emblem, inspired by the ancient Olympic Games, reflecting ideals of strength and competition.

Olympiacos is the most successful club in Greek football history, holding records for league titles, domestic cups, and overall trophies. The team has won dozens of national championships and has often dominated the domestic scene, especially in long periods of sustained success. It is also one of the most popular clubs in Greece, with a large fan base and strong rivalries, particularly with Panathinaikos in the famous “Derby of the Eternal Enemies.”

On the international stage, Olympiacos has been the most successful Greek club in European competitions. The club made history by winning the UEFA Europa Conference League in the 2023–24 season, becoming the first Greek team to claim a major European trophy. This achievement further strengthened its reputation as the leading representative of Greek football in Europe.

name: Panathinaikos FC
content:
Panathinaikos FC is a professional football club based in Athens, Greece, founded in 1908 by Giorgos Kalafatis. It is one of the oldest and most historic clubs in Greek football and has never been relegated from the top division. The club is part of the wider Panathinaikos athletic organization and traditionally plays in green and white, earning the nickname “The Greens.”

Panathinaikos is one of the most successful teams in Greece, with numerous domestic titles including league championships and Greek Cups, as well as several domestic doubles. The club has a large fan base and maintains a fierce rivalry with Olympiacos, with matches between them known as the “Derby of the Eternal Enemies,” one of the most intense rivalries in European football.

On the international stage, Panathinaikos holds a unique place in Greek football history. It is the only Greek club to have reached a European Cup (now UEFA Champions League) final, doing so in 1971, and has also reached the semi-finals on multiple occasions. These achievements made it one of the most recognized Greek teams in European competitions and a key representative of the country’s football abroad.

name: AEK Athens FC
content:
AEK Athens FC is a professional football club based in Athens, Greece, founded in 1924 by Greek refugees from Constantinople following the Greco-Turkish War. The club’s name, which translates to “Athletic Union of Constantinople,” reflects its origins and cultural identity. It has since become one of the most important and historically significant clubs in Greek football, playing its home matches in Nea Filadelfeia.

AEK is among the most successful teams in Greece, winning numerous domestic trophies, including league championships and Greek Cups. It is notable for being the only Greek club to have won all major competitions organized by the national federation. Alongside Olympiacos and Panathinaikos, AEK forms part of the traditional “big three” of Greek football, with strong rivalries and a large national fan base.

On the international stage, AEK Athens has achieved several notable milestones for Greek football. It was one of the first Greek clubs to make a deep run in European competitions, reaching the quarter-finals of the European Cup in 1969 and later the semi-finals of the UEFA Cup in the 1970s. Although it has not won a major European trophy, the club has consistently represented Greece in continental tournaments and remains a prominent presence in both domestic and international football.

name: PAOK FC
content:
PAOK FC is a professional football club based in Thessaloniki, Greece, founded in 1926 by Greek refugees from Constantinople following the Greco-Turkish War. The club’s full name reflects these origins, and its emblem, the double-headed eagle, symbolizes its historical and cultural roots. PAOK plays its home matches at Toumba Stadium and is one of the most popular and widely supported teams in northern Greece.

Domestically, PAOK is considered one of the major clubs in Greek football. It has won multiple league titles, including championships in 1976, 1985, 2019, and 2024, as well as several Greek Cups. One of its greatest achievements came in the 2018–19 season, when the team won the league undefeated and secured a historic domestic double, marking the most successful period in the club’s history.

In recent years, PAOK has remained competitive both domestically and in European competitions. Under the ownership of Ivan Savvidis since 2012, the club stabilized financially and achieved consistent success, including cup victories and strong European runs. The team continues to be a key force in Greek football, regularly challenging for titles and representing the country in continental tournaments.

name: Aris Thessaloniki FC
content:
Aris Thessaloniki FC is a professional football club based in Thessaloniki, Greece, founded in 1914. It is one of the oldest and most historic clubs in the country and was a founding member of key football organizations in Greece. The club is named after Ares, the ancient Greek god of war, and its traditional colors are yellow and black, reflecting regional and historical symbolism.

Aris was one of the dominant teams in Greek football during the interwar period, winning several national championships, including titles in 1928, 1932, and 1946. Over time, it established itself as one of the major clubs in Greece, with a strong fan base and a long-standing presence in the top division. Although it has not matched the trophy count of the country’s biggest clubs, it remains an important and respected part of Greek football history.

In European competitions, Aris has had several notable appearances, including participation in the UEFA Cup and Europa League, with its best runs reaching the later knockout stages and group phases. The club has also been known for strong home performances and memorable victories against well-known European teams. Today, Aris continues to compete in the Super League Greece, aiming to remain competitive domestically while maintaining its historical identity and passionate support.

name: AE Larissa FC
content:
Athlitiki Enosi Larissa FC, commonly known as AEL or Larissa, is a professional football club based in the city of Larissa in Greece. It was founded in 1964 through the merger of several local clubs, with the aim of creating a strong team to represent the region of Thessaly. The club’s colors are crimson and white, and its emblem features a rearing horse, symbolizing strength and regional identity.

AEL is historically significant as the most successful provincial club in Greek football. Its greatest achievement came in the 1987–88 season, when it won the national league title, becoming the only team from outside Athens and Thessaloniki to do so. The club also won the Greek Cup twice, in 1985 and 2007, during what is considered its most successful periods.

In addition to domestic success, Larissa has participated in European competitions, with its best result being a run to the quarter-finals of the Cup Winners’ Cup in 1984–85. Over the years, the club has experienced periods of decline, including relegations and financial difficulties, but has also achieved several promotions back to higher divisions. Despite these fluctuations, AEL remains an important and recognizable name in Greek football.

name: Iraklis FC
content:
Iraklis FC is a historic football club based in Thessaloniki, Greece, with roots dating back to 1899 through a cultural organization that later developed a sports section. The football team itself emerged in the early 20th century, and the club officially adopted the name “Iraklis” in 1910, inspired by the ancient Greek hero Heracles. It is considered one of the oldest clubs in Greek football and one of the earliest established in Thessaloniki.

Throughout its history, Iraklis has been an important but less decorated club compared to Greece’s biggest teams. Before the establishment of a nationwide league, it achieved success in regional competitions in Macedonia. Its main domestic achievement came in 1976, when it won the Greek Cup, and it has also reached several other cup finals. Internationally, the club won the Balkans Cup in 1985, marking its most notable success outside Greece.

In modern times, Iraklis has faced significant financial and administrative difficulties, leading to relegations and instability. Despite these challenges, it remains a well-known and respected club with a loyal fan base and a strong historical identity in Greek football. Although it has not consistently competed at the highest level in recent years, its legacy as one of the country’s traditional clubs continues to be recognized.

name: Apollon Smyrnis FC
content:
Apollon Smyrnis FC is a historic Greek football club based in Athens, with origins dating back to 1891 in the city of Smyrna. It is one of the oldest sports institutions connected to Greek football, and its football section was established in 1910. Following the population exchanges of the early 20th century, the club relocated to Athens, where it continued its activities and became part of the Greek football system.

Throughout its history, Apollon Smyrnis has been a respected but not dominant force in Greek football. The club has spent many seasons in the top division and achieved notable results, including finishing third in the league in 1963 and reaching the Greek Cup final in 1996. It has also won several lower-division titles, highlighting periods of promotion and rebuilding.

In modern times, the club has experienced fluctuations between divisions, reflecting financial and sporting challenges. Despite this instability, Apollon Smyrnis remains an important historical club with a strong identity rooted in its Smyrna heritage. It continues to be recognized for its long tradition, loyal supporters, and role in the development of Greek football.

name: Panionios FC
content:
Panionios FC is a historic Greek football club based in Nea Smyrni, Athens, with origins dating back to 1890 in the city of Smyrna. It was originally part of a broader athletic and cultural organization and is considered one of the oldest clubs connected to Greek sport. After the events of the Greco-Turkish War and the population exchange in the early 1920s, the club relocated to Greece, where it continued its activities and became part of the national football system.

Throughout its history, Panionios has been regarded as an important but not dominant force in Greek football. The club has achieved notable success, including winning the Greek Cup twice and finishing as runner-up in the national championship on several occasions. It also enjoyed international recognition by winning the Balkans Cup in 1971 and reaching the quarter-finals of a European competition in the late 1990s.

In modern times, Panionios has experienced fluctuations between divisions and financial challenges, which have affected its competitiveness. Despite this, it remains a respected club known for its strong youth development and contribution to Greek football. Today, it continues to compete in the lower tiers while maintaining its long-standing tradition and historical identity.

name: Ethnikos Piraeus FC
content:
Ethnikos Piraeus FC is a historic Greek football club based in Piraeus, founded in 1923 through a series of mergers between local teams before adopting its current name in 1924. It is one of the traditional clubs of Greek football and was among the founding members of the Hellenic Football Federation. In its early years, the club established itself as a strong competitor, reaching the final stage of the first national championship and winning the Greek Cup in 1933.

The club enjoyed some of its best performances in the mid-20th century, finishing as runner-up in the national championship in 1928 and 1956. It was also close to winning the title in 1957, but a controversial punishment prevented it from competing fairly for the championship. For many decades, Ethnikos remained a stable top-division team, maintaining a long حضور in the highest level of Greek football before eventually facing decline.

From the 1990s onward, the club experienced significant difficulties, including relegations, financial problems, and periods spent in lower divisions. Despite occasional promotions and attempts to rebuild, it has not returned to the top tier since the late 1990s. Today, Ethnikos Piraeus continues to compete in the lower levels of Greek football, but it remains an important historical club with a notable legacy in the country’s sporting history.

name: OFI Crete FC
content:
OFI Crete FC is a professional football club based in Heraklion on the island of Crete, Greece. It was founded in 1925 by a group of local athletes and takes its name from “Omilos Filathlon Irakleiou,” meaning Heraklion Sports Club. The team is part of a larger multi-sport organization and plays its home matches at the Theodoros Vardinogiannis Stadium.

Historically, OFI developed as the strongest club from Crete and spent many years climbing through the Greek football system. After competing mainly in regional football in its early decades, it eventually reached the national divisions and established itself in the top tier in the late 1960s. Since the mid-1970s, the club has generally remained a regular participant in Greece’s highest leagues, building a reputation as a stable provincial side outside the traditional Athens and Thessaloniki power centers.

The club’s greatest achievements include winning the Greek Cup in the 1986–87 season and the Balkans Cup in 1989, along with several appearances in European competitions. In modern times, OFI continues to compete in the top division, balancing periods of stability with rebuilding phases, while remaining one of the most important and recognizable football clubs in Crete.

name: Atromitos FC
content:
Atromitos FC is a professional football club based in Peristeri, a suburb of Athens, Greece. It was founded in 1923 by local students and quickly became part of the early development of organized football in the country. The club plays its home matches at Peristeri Stadium and competes in the Super League Greece, the top tier of Greek football.

Throughout its history, Atromitos has been considered a strong mid-to-upper level Greek club, especially in the modern era. It has reached the Greek Cup final twice in 2011 and 2012 and has also achieved high league finishes, including multiple fourth-place and a notable third-place finish in its early championship history. These results established the club as a consistent competitor outside the traditional “big three” teams.

In European competitions, Atromitos has regularly participated in UEFA tournaments, including Europa League qualifying rounds, where it has recorded mixed but competitive results against stronger international opponents. Since the 2010s, the club has maintained its status as a stable top-flight side in Greece, focusing on competitive league performance and occasional European qualification campaigns.

name: Asteras Tripolis FC
content:
Asteras Tripolis FC is a professional football club based in Tripoli, in the Arcadia region of Greece. It was founded in 1931 and is currently one of the established teams in the Super League Greece. The club plays its home matches at the Theodoros Kolokotronis Stadium and is known for its yellow and blue identity as well as its rapid rise through the Greek football divisions in the 2000s.

The club’s modern era is defined by a strong rise from the lower tiers to the top division within a short period. After significant progress in the early 2000s, Asteras reached the Super League in 2007 and quickly became a stable mid-table and upper-mid-table side. It also achieved notable success in the Greek Cup, reaching the final in 2013 and several semi-final appearances, establishing itself as one of the strongest provincial clubs in the country.

In European competitions, Asteras has represented Greece in the UEFA Europa League, including group stage appearances, marking an important milestone for a club of its size. Over time, it has built a reputation for organization, competitiveness, and consistent performances against stronger opponents. The club continues to compete in the top division, aiming to remain a regular contender in domestic and occasional European competitions.

name: Kastoria 1980 FC
content:
Kastoria 1980 FC is a Greek football club based in the city of Kastoria in Western Macedonia. The club was formed in 1963 through the merger of three local teams, aiming to create a stronger representative side for the region. It plays its home matches at the Municipal Stadium of Kastoria and is commonly known by its nickname related to the city’s historic fur trade identity.

The club’s most important achievement came in 1980, when it won the Greek Cup, defeating Iraklis in the final. This victory marked one of the most remarkable moments in its history, as it was the club’s first major national title and a rare success for a provincial team outside Greece’s largest football centers. Kastoria also competed in the Greek top division during several periods, especially in the 1970s and 1980s.

In European competition, Kastoria participated in the Cup Winners’ Cup following its cup triumph, although its run was short-lived. Over time, the club experienced fluctuations between divisions and financial difficulties, including periods of decline and restructuring. Despite these challenges, it remains remembered for its historic cup victory and its unique place in Greek football history as a small club that achieved national success.

name: Doxa Drama FC
content:
Doxa Drama FC is a Greek football club based in the city of Drama in northern Greece. It was founded in 1918, originally under the name Peleus, before being renamed Doxa, meaning “Glory.” The club emerged during a period when football was spreading in the region and is considered one of the historic teams of Greek football. It plays its home matches at the Doxa Drama Stadium and is known by the nickname “Black Eagles.”

In its early and mid-20th century history, Doxa Drama became one of the stronger provincial clubs in Greece. It was a founding member of the country’s top national league and reached the Greek Cup final three times in the 1950s, although it did not manage to win the trophy. The club spent many seasons in the top division, building a reputation as a competitive side, especially before the rise of larger metropolitan clubs.

Over time, financial and administrative problems led to periods of decline, including relegations to lower divisions and long spells outside the top flight. Despite these difficulties, Doxa Drama has experienced several promotions and continues to compete in the Greek football system. The club remains an important part of Greek football history, particularly known for its early achievements and traditional identity.

name: SFK Pierikos
content:
SFK Pierikos is a Greek football club based in Katerini, founded on 11 April 1961 through the merger of two local teams, Megas Alexandros Katerinis and Olympos Katerinis. The creation of the club aimed to unite the city’s football strength into a single competitive side capable of reaching the national level. It quickly established itself as the main football representative of the Pieria region.

In its early history, Pierikos achieved rapid progress, gaining promotion to the top division soon after its formation. The club spent several seasons in Greece’s first tier during the 1960s and 1970s and even reached the Greek Cup final in 1963, where it faced one of the country’s strongest teams. Over time, it became known as a competitive side that often moved between divisions but could challenge stronger opponents on its day.

In later decades, Pierikos experienced frequent promotions and relegations, spending most of its time in the second and lower divisions. Despite financial and sporting difficulties, the club has remained active in the Greek football system and continues to represent Katerini. Its history is marked by early success, occasional strong campaigns, and a long-standing role as a traditional regional club in Greek football.

name: Athinaikos FC
content:
Athinaikos FC is a Greek football club based in the suburb of Vyronas in Athens. It was founded in 1917 and is part of the wider Athinaikos multi-sport organization. The club is known for its red and yellow colours and is historically linked with the development of sport in the Athens metropolitan area. Over time, it has remained a representative team of its local community.

Throughout its history, Athinaikos has mostly competed in the lower and mid levels of Greek football, with occasional appearances in the top division. Its most successful period came in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when it reached the Greek Cup final and established itself as a competitive first-division side. One of its most notable achievements was a European appearance in the early 1990s, where it faced Manchester United in the Cup Winners’ Cup, marking the club’s most memorable international moment.

In later years, the club experienced financial difficulties and fluctuating sporting fortunes, leading to relegations and time spent in lower divisions. Despite this, Athinaikos has remained active in Greek football and continues to compete at regional and national levels. It is still recognized as a traditional Athenian club with a long history and strong local identity.

name: Ionikos FC
content:
Ionikos FC is a Greek football club based in Nikaia, a suburb of Piraeus in Athens. It was founded in 1965 through the merger of two local clubs and gradually developed into one of the more recognizable teams in Greek football. The club plays its home matches at the Neapoli Stadium and is known for its blue and white colours.

Throughout its history, Ionikos has experienced periods of steady rise and strong performances, especially from the late 1980s onward. After earning promotion to the top division in 1989, the club spent many seasons in the Greek first tier, even finishing as high as fifth place and reaching the Greek Cup final in 2000. It also participated in European competition, marking the peak of its sporting success.

In later years, Ionikos went through financial instability and multiple relegations, dropping into lower divisions at times. Despite these difficulties, the club has repeatedly rebuilt itself and returned to higher levels of competition. It remains a traditional Athens-area club with a loyal fan base and a history of competing in both domestic and occasional European tournaments.

name: Xanthi FC
content:
Xanthi FC is a Greek football club based in the city of Xanthi in Thrace. It was formed in 1967 through the merger of two local clubs, Aspida Xanthi and Orfeas Xanthi, as part of an effort to unify the city’s football scene. The club gradually established itself as the main sporting representative of the region and built a reputation for developing local talent and maintaining a stable presence in national competitions.

For many years, Xanthi competed mainly in the lower tiers of Greek football before rising steadily through the system. It reached the top division in 1989 and later became a consistent Super League side, often finishing in mid-table positions but occasionally achieving stronger seasons. The club also gained recognition for its organization and professional structure, especially after becoming privately managed in the 1990s.

In European competitions, Xanthi made several appearances in UEFA tournaments, including Europa League qualifying rounds in the 2000s and 2010s. However, in recent years the club faced serious financial and ownership problems that led to instability and eventual withdrawal from professional competition in 2022. Despite this decline, Xanthi remains an important name in Greek football history, known for its modern-era competitiveness and regional significance.
